Age of Aquarius
AYJ uv uh-KWAIR-ee-us
noun (Boomer slang)
From astrology: the slow precession of the equinoxes moves the sun’s position at the spring equinox backward through the zodiac, roughly one sign every two thousand years, and astrologers taught that the "Age of Pisces" was ending and the "Age of Aquarius" — an era of harmony, brotherhood, and spiritual awakening — was dawning. The phrase was popularized by the rock musical Hair (off-Broadway 1967, Broadway 1968), whose opening song "Aquarius" proclaimed it, and by the 5th Dimension’s medley "Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In" (No. 1, 1969). It became a byword for the New Age movement.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Age of Aquarius was the hippie’s promised new era: an astrological age of peace, love, harmony, and spiritual enlightenment that was supposedly dawning in the late 1960s, announced by the musical Hair and sung on every radio in 1969. The Christian observation: the phrase is astrology dressed as hope, and Scripture is plain about both. Of astrology, the prophet mocks Babylon’s reliance on it: "Let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up, and save thee from these things that shall come upon thee. Behold, they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them" (Isa 47:13–14). "Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them" (Jer 10:2). Israel was forbidden any "observer of times" (Deu 18:10). The stars do not govern history; they declare their Maker: "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork" (Psa 19:1). Of hope, Scripture says a new age has indeed dawned, but not by the movement of constellations. The only star that ever announced an age pointed the wise men to a manger: "we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him" (Mat 2:2). The age of harmony and brotherhood the song longed for is the kingdom of Christ, begun at His first coming and consummated at His second. The Age of Aquarius did not arrive in 1969; the kingdom of God arrived in Bethlehem, and it is still advancing.

Webster 1828 Definition

Astrological "new age" of harmony said to be dawning in the late 1960s, popularized by Hair (1967–68) and "Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In" (1969) — astrology Scripture forbids (Isa 47:13–14; Deu 18:10), set against the star that led to Christ (Mat 2:2).

AGE OF AQUARIUS, n. (astrological; Boomer-era popularization 1967–69) In astrology, an era of about two thousand years associated with the sign Aquarius, believed by its proponents to bring peace, harmony, and spiritual awakening; hence the New Age hopes of the 1960s counterculture.

Webster (1828) — AQUARIUS, noun [Latin] The water bearer; a sign in the zodiac which the sun enters about the 21st day of January; so called from the rains which prevail at that season, in Italy and the East. The stars in this constellation according to Ptolenty, are 45; according to Tycho Brahe, 41; according to Hevelius, 45; and according to Flamstead, 108.

Decode for families: horoscopes, zodiac apps, and "what’s your sign?" are the Age of Aquarius still on the shelf. Teach Psa 19:1.

Key Scripture

Isa 47:13 — "Thou art wearied in the multitude of thy counsels. Let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up, and save thee from these things that shall come upon thee."

Isa 47:14 — "Behold, they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them; they shall not deliver themselves from the power of the flame: there shall not be a coal to warm at, nor fire to sit before it."

Jer 10:2 — "Thus saith the LORD, Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them."

Deu 18:10 — "There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch,"

Psa 19:1 — "To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork."

Mat 2:2 — "Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him."

Modern Corruption

The Age of Aquarius promised a new era of harmony governed by the stars; Scripture forbids astrology, makes the stars heralds of God’s glory, and locates the new age in the kingdom of Christ.

expand to see more

Hair was a musical about draft resistance, drugs, and free love, and its opening anthem baptized all of it in astrology. The counterculture’s turn to the stars was part of a larger turn from the church to every alternative religion available — tarot, the I Ching, Eastern mysticism, the occult. That turn did not fade with the 1960s; it became the New Age movement and lives on in the horoscope apps of today. Scripture’s verdict has not changed: the astrologers cannot save (Isa 47:13), and God’s people are not to be dismayed at the signs of heaven (Jer 10:2).

There is a better reading of the sky. The heavens declare God’s glory (Psa 19:1), and once a star led seekers from the East to the true King (Mat 2:2). The wise men left their astrology at the manger and worshiped. Every seeker who has looked to the stars for meaning can be invited to do the same.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin Aquarius (water-bearer) → zodiac sign → astrological "Age of Aquarius" (precession of the equinoxes) → Hair (1967–68) → 1969 No. 1 hit → New Age movement.

1969: the 5th Dimension, "Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In," No. 1
